claim: Selective search with heuristics, not speed, is what makes problem solving tractable; blind search is hopeless.
agent_test: Compare blind sampling of N candidates vs heuristic-ordered generation at equal tokens on a task with a coded checker.

claim: A problem is a space of states plus operators plus a goal test; solving is constructing states by applying operators. A scaffold that makes state, operator and test explicit as code objects matches the theory.
agent_test: Ablate explicit state and test objects (prose-only vs structured) at equal tokens.

claim: Tree search over model-generated thoughts beats plain chain prompts by a large margin on tasks with a checkable step state and weak baselines (Game of 24: 4% CoT to 74% ToT; Blocksworld 6-step 0.00 to 0.42). Caveat from matched-budget work: with GPT-3.5 ToT lost to self-consistency (d01), and with a learned verifier tree search beat verifier-weighted voting by only about 0 to 4 points on GSM8K (d17).
agent_test: Run ToT-style search vs best-of-N CoT at equal tokens on our own checkable tasks.

claim: The search gain is conditional: on tasks the model already does well (GSM8K CoT 86 vs ToT 90, StrategyQA 82 vs 83) or against strong voting baselines (GSM8K RAP(10) 51.6 vs CoT+SC(10) 46.8) the gain is small.
agent_test: Gate: run a cheap pass first; spend search only when the checker fails. Measure share escalated and net gain.

claim: ToT is not cheaper than best-of-N in dollars at its reported setting: $0.74 vs $0.47 (CoT best of 100) per case, with fewer completion tokens (5.5k vs 6.7k). Creative Writing ToT costs about 5x CoT. The earlier summary 'less than brute-force sampling' was wrong in dollars.
agent_test: Report dollars and calls, not only completion tokens, in every arm.

claim: Pruning and backtracking carry the search gain on deeper tasks: crosswords game-level 20% ToT vs 5% without pruning and 5% without backtracking.
agent_test: Ablate backtrack and prune in our scaffold on a depth>=5 task (all from the one ToT paper).

claim: The value or evaluation function is a key component; generation, not evaluation, is the bottleneck on Game of 24 (GPT-4 gen + GPT-3.5 eval 64%; reverse 31%); an open-model re-run shows a better value function nearly closes the BFS-1 vs BFS-5 gap; LATS without LM heuristic 0.37 vs 0.63.
agent_test: Swap evaluator quality (self-judge vs code check vs stronger model) at fixed generator and tokens.

claim: Gains depend on the model: GPT-3.5 ToT 19% vs GPT-4 74% on Game of 24; weaker proposers lose most of the gain. New: Llemma-7B plus a reward-guided tree search beat Llemma-34B (d04), and ToT with a GPT-3.5 proposer fell to 0.38 even with a GPT-4 evaluator (d02). Direction depends on whether the small model must also judge its thoughts.
agent_test: Test the scaffold on the smaller model we will actually deploy.

claim: An external sound verifier in a generate-test loop works (Blocksworld 82% with VAL back-prompting); the model's own self-critique does not (graph coloring 1 of 100 correct under self-critique vs 16% baseline; GSM8K self-correction 75.9 to 74.7).
agent_test: Compare code-verifier feedback vs self-critique vs plain resampling at equal tokens.

claim: Feedback richness did not matter beyond a sound check: binary vs full error list made no significant difference, and n=15 resampling reached about the same 40%.
agent_test: Check whether richer feedback beats plain resampling on our tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Writing the successor function and goal test once as code, then running ordinary search, solves benchmark sets at 100% in few LLM calls (Game of 24 1361/1361), far cheaper than LLM-in-the-loop search (estimated $14,000 RAP, $16,000 LATS vs $40 CoT across four datasets). First-try failure: the successor function needed 1.2 to 2.8 tries with GPT-4 (d06); with automatic tests, GPT-4o needed 2.0 to 5.8 calls and GPT-4o-mini 4.8 to 10 against a minimum of 2 (d08). All domains had exact short rule texts.
agent_test: Generate operators and goal test as code from the problem statement; compare with prompted search at equal cost.

claim: Representation changes difficulty: object-based encoding raised GPT-4 ARC solved from 13 to 23 of 50; human Tower of Hanoi completion rises with an external display (5-disk 93% vs 63% Exp 1; 87.4% vs 55.3% Exp 2).
agent_test: Try 2-3 encodings per item (grid vs objects vs code state) at equal tokens. Classic isomorph effects (Kotovsky 1985, Simon-Hayes) were never opened, so effect sizes are missing.

claim: Mental-then-external transfer (4-disk solved mentally helped later 5-disk, 79.3% vs 65.4%, p=.0488) is fragile: borderline, and absent in Exp 1 (p=.57).
agent_test: Do not build on it.

claim: Long-reasoning models improve Blocksworld a lot (o1-preview 97.8% vs 62.6% best plain LLM) but drop under renaming (52.8%, 37.3%) and with plan length (23.63% at 20-40 steps), and flag only 27% of unsolvable cases.
agent_test: Include renamed-surface and unsolvable variants in our evaluation to detect pattern matching.

claim: Reported 'collapse' of reasoning models on Hanoi and River Crossing is partly an artifact of output limits and impossible River Crossing instances; a generating-function format restores accuracy (preliminary, informal).
agent_test: Compare move-list output vs program output vs tool-per-move on Hanoi N up to 12 at equal tokens.

claim: Even with a state-tracking environment (one tool call per move) or the algorithm in the prompt, models still failed past a size threshold; stepwise prompting delayed collapse only a little. Counter-evidence: with the strategy and the current state in each prompt, single-move calls and per-step voting solved 20-disk Hanoi (about 1.05 million moves) with zero errors in one reported run (d10); this is a different design from a tool-per-move environment.
agent_test: Have the program hold the state and apply moves; the model only picks. Test beyond N=8.

claim: One-pass in-context algorithmic traces (AoT) matched ToT with 1 query (71% vs 69% when re-run by the AoT authors; ToT's own report 74%).
agent_test: Compare AoT-style prompt vs controller-driven ToT at equal tokens; no independent replication found.

claim: Training on whole search traces with dead ends beat training on optimal paths only (Countdown 51.27% vs 25.73%), but this is training, outside our no-training constraint.
agent_test: Not testable without training; informs only what trace formats to show in context.

claim: Soar impasse-driven substates give an automatic switch from fast rule knowledge to slow deliberate search; LLMs can draft Soar problem-space specs but need a critic that runs the rules (86%+ success, 25+ points over one-shot).
agent_test: Trigger escalation to deliberate search by explicit impasse (no applicable operator, tie, failed test), not by model confidence.

claim: Human difficulty on transformation puzzles is not explained by solution length or state-space size; a random-plus-greedy walk model predicts better (Rush Hour rho .90, Sokoban .61 vs .41).
agent_test: Predict item difficulty from simple features to allocate budget; test on our tasks.

claim: Reaching an impasse does not by itself produce insight; representational change is the rival mechanism to pure search, and ill-defined problems are absent from all LLM search benchmarks.
agent_test: Include insight-type tasks (matchstick, eight-coin) and compare search-only vs a forced restructure operator.

claim: Plain repeated sampling is a strong baseline whenever an automatic checker exists: coverage rises log-linearly with samples (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% at 1 sample to 56% at 250; MATH Llama-3-8B 82.9% at 100 to 98.44% at 10,000), but without a checker, voting and reward models plateau. A cheap model in a verifier loop can match a reasoning model for less money (calendar: o1-mini $2.70 for 94% vs GPT-4o-mini loop $2.48 for 97%).
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare best-of-N plus coded checker against tree search with the same checker on our task mix; report coverage and picked-answer accuracy separately.

claim: Step-by-step text helps mostly on math, symbolic and logic tasks (avg CoT gain 14.2 / 12.3 / 6.9 points) and not elsewhere (56.8 vs 56.1); CoT gains on Blocksworld come from prompts matched to the problem class and shrink as instances grow past the examples. A symbolic solver or tool beats CoT on symbolic work.
agent_test: Gate: skip multi-step scaffolding on items with no symbolic step; measure accuracy and tokens saved on a mixed set.

claim: Best-first tree search over real environment states raises web-agent success and scales with search budget (VWA GPT-4o 18.9 to 26.4; budget c=20 on a 200-task subset 24.5 to 37.0), but the 37.0 depends on self-consistency in the value function (28.5 without) and costs up to 20x more LM calls per search iteration. Weaker model gains most in relative terms (Llama-3-70B 7.6 to 16.7).
agent_test: Add a budget curve (c = 0,5,10,20) and a value-function-with-vs-without-voting ablation on one multi-step tool task.

claim: The same state space can differ in difficulty by large factors depending on how moves are represented: Hayes-Simon isomorphs about 2:1, Kotovsky-Hayes-Simon isomorphs up to 16:1 (secondhand), Chinese Ring Puzzle vs digital isomorph 79.7 vs 13-20 minutes with 24 of 41 failing in two hours; difficulty lives in the cost of testing move legality (entities to image), and training on the move operator removes the gap.
agent_test: Re-render the same item with 2-3 encodings and with a worked move-demonstration; check whether a move-legality check step closes the gap.

claim: State-space size and solution length do not set human difficulty on linear or small spaces: starting 21 vs 31 moves out gave no reliable time difference (F(1,53)=2.12, p<.2); behaviour is long unproductive stretches then a fast run; misleading progress heuristics (balls out of boxes) trap solvers.
agent_test: Predict item difficulty from simple features (progress-heuristic misleads, move-test cost) and use it to set effort; compare with length-based allocation.

claim: Humans do not keep a perfect goal stack: goal retrieval time rises with how long ago the goal was set and goals can be lost; people request to see the stack only 1-5% of the time. Subgoal stacks need external storage.
agent_test: Compare keeping the goal stack in a written state object that is re-read each step against implicit stack in context, on 5+ depth tasks.

claim: Several different strategies solve the same puzzle (goal recursion, perceptual, rote move pattern) and people do not start with goal recursion; rote strategies break when rules change. Strategy identity is not visible from solution correctness.
agent_test: Log which strategy the agent used on isomorph variants; test whether a rote-pattern solver fails on rule changes.

claim: Pure means-ends analysis was not enough: it needs a hand-written difference table, and humans switched to abstract planning bursts (Planning GPS); selectivity buys speed at lost completeness (MATER branching about 20 to 2; waypoints cut search from b^L to k*b^(L/k)).
agent_test: Plan-in-abstract-then-fill vs flat step generation at equal tokens on tasks with 6+ steps.

claim: Think-aloud verbalisation is nonreactive on accuracy (r=-.03 over 94 studies, about 3,500 participants), while explaining or describing is reactive and raises performance, but verbal overshadowing on insight problems is contested (one study about 25 point drop, replications smaller or none).
agent_test: Compare plain trace vs forced explain-each-step at equal tokens; keep insight items separate.

claim: Insight difficulty tracks how far a constraint must be relaxed and how tight a chunk is (matchstick medians 40 / 155 / 300 / 140 s for types A-D, N=20), supporting representational change as a separate mechanism from search; one task family, small N.
agent_test: Test a forced restructure step on matchstick-type items vs more sampling at equal tokens.

claim: Collapse past a size threshold appears across 2025-26 frontier reasoning models on parameterised puzzles with validators (Hanoi level 4 collapses most models) and models lose intermediate state in 3-disk Hanoi games; whether this is capability or output-format artifact remains disputed.
agent_test: Run the program-held-state vs model-held-state comparison from A02.01-K16 at sizes straddling the threshold, with counts.

claim: A separate controller that holds state and a rule checker around the LLM, with backtracking, solves small Sudoku grids (3x3 10/10, 4x4 9/10, 5x5 8/10) far above few-shot CoT; N is 10 per size and the paper is not peer reviewed.
agent_test: Replicate with larger N; compare controller with coded checker to resampling with the same checker.

claim: MCTS with trained critics raised Llama-2-70B GSM8K from 73.7 greedy to 88.9, but part of the gain is training; not available to a scaffold-only agent.
agent_test: Not testable without training; only informs which critic signals to imitate in prompts.

claim: Search against sampling at equal compute is mixed, not settled. Naive MCTS with a reward model lost to plain sampling at every FLOP budget (d03); a budget-aware reward-guided tree search beat sampling with about 7x less compute (d03); with a learned verifier tree search edged verifier-weighted voting by about 0 to 4 points on GSM8K at more tokens (d17); ToT beat strategies at GPT-4 but lost to self-consistency at GPT-3.5 on Game of 24 (d01). No paper runs a coded goal test against best-of-N with the same coded verifier.
agent_test: At equal dollars, run (a) best-of-N with the coded checker, (b) generate-test-repair loop, (c) tree search with the same checker, on our task mix. Report cost per solved item.

claim: Search gain is tied to evaluator quality and the proposer: a random evaluator sharply lowered ToT accuracy, evaluating once instead of three times also lowered it, a GPT-3.5 evaluator kept 72% against 76% for GPT-4 at about a fifth of the cost, and a GPT-3.5 proposer with a GPT-4 evaluator got 0.38 (d02). No study swaps the tree for resampling with the same evaluator.
agent_test: Hold evaluator fixed (coded check, self-judge). Compare tree, beam, and plain resampling at the same token cost.

claim: Search helps on mid-difficulty items and can hurt on easy ones: beam search with a process verifier degraded with more budget on easy MATH levels 1-2, beat best-of-N on levels 3-4, and did nothing on level 5; difficulty-based allocation matched best-of-N with up to 4x less compute (d05). A second paper found REBASE equal to sampling on easy levels and ahead on hard (d04). Supports gating by a cheap first pass.
agent_test: Bin items by cheap-pass agreement; escalate only mid bins; check accuracy does not fall on the easy bin.

claim: Generated operator code usually needs repair: successor functions took 1.2 to 2.8 tries with GPT-4 and a human (d06); with automatic tests GPT-4o averaged 2.0 to 5.8 calls and smaller models up to 10 (cap) on five puzzle domains (d08). Errors were mainly unsound or incomplete successors (d09). Transfer to messy tasks with fuzzy rules is untested.
agent_test: Generate operators and goal tests as code for 3 non-puzzle tasks; log first-try pass rate against hand-written tests.

claim: Hanoi-style collapse is not a hard limit if each step is small and checked: with the strategy and current state in every prompt, single-move calls and first-to-ahead-by-k voting solved 20-disk Hanoi (about 1.05 million moves) with zero errors in one reported run, per-step error stable from 10 to 20 disks, errors decorrelated, small non-reasoning models as good per step as reasoning ones (d10, d11). It tests execution of a given algorithm, not discovery.
agent_test: Measure per-step error p on our small model; vote only if p is above 0.5; compare move-list output with voted single-step calls.

claim: A few worked examples close most of a representation gap for LLMs: GPT-4 two-digit addition in base 9 went from 38.6% at 0-shot to 85.8% at 8-shot, against 98.2% in base 10 (d18). This is the nearest LLM analogue of move-demonstration effects; no study tests operator-compatibility transfer.
agent_test: On a puzzle with two encodings, add 2 worked moves or an explicit legality check; measure accuracy gain per token.

claim: On insight-type riddles models are far below people (7.6% non-reasoning, 17.6% reasoning vs 52.9% human) and 5 to 39% of wrong answers had the correct candidate in the trace but were not endorsed (d13). That favours an external verify-and-stop step over a forced restructure operator; the restructure operator itself is untested. A mental-set study with six items per cell (d12) is too small to use.
agent_test: On riddle or matchstick items, compare forced restructure, more sampling, and sampling plus a candidate-checking step at equal tokens.

claim: Verbalised confidence is a poor escalation trigger: values cluster at 80 to 100% and failure-prediction AUROC was about 0.52 for black-box and 0.61 for the best white-box method (d14). A trained step-level router beat a binary switch (d15) but no study compares impasse triggers with confidence triggers in a prompt scaffold.
agent_test: Escalate on explicit signals (failed check, no legal operator, repeated state) vs on stated confidence; compare cost and accuracy.

claim: Explicit subgoals in the prompt help long-horizon agents, and dropping the detail of finished subgoals helps further (tyreworld success 10% standard, 40% subgoal-only, 60% with summarised subgoal memory; ablation on one task) (d16). No study tests a written goal stack at depth 5 or more against the implicit stack.
agent_test: Depth-controlled task (nested subgoals 3, 5, 8): written re-read stack vs implicit, equal tokens.
